title: Constitution (1st Amendment) Act, 1951
description: The 1st Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1951. Added special provisions for advancement of socially and educationally backward classes of citizens. Established the Ninth Schedule to protect certain laws from judicial review. Added Articles 31A and 31B. Amended Articles 15, 19, 85, 87, 174, 176, 341, 342, 372, 376.

title: Constitution (2nd Amendment) Act, 1953
description: The 2nd Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1953. Readjusted the scale of representation in the House of the People by removing the upper limit of 7,50,000 for a parliamentary constituency.

title: Constitution (3rd Amendment) Act, 1955
description: The 3rd Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1955. Amended the Seventh Schedule (Concurrent List) regarding trade and commerce in, and the production, supply and distribution of essential commodities.

title: Constitution (4th Amendment) Act, 1955
description: The 4th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1955. Amended Articles 31, 31A and the Ninth Schedule. Addressed compulsory acquisition of private property by the State and compensation provisions.

title: Constitution (5th Amendment) Act, 1955
description: The 5th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1955. Empowered the President to fix a time limit for states to express views on proposed laws affecting state boundaries and areas under Article 3.

title: Constitution (6th Amendment) Act, 1956
description: The 6th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1956. Amended Articles 269 and 286 relating to taxes on the sale or purchase of goods in inter-state trade. Added new entries to Union List and State List.

title: Constitution (7th Amendment) Act, 1956
description: The 7th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1956. Major reorganization of states on linguistic lines. Abolished the classification of states into Parts A, B, C, and D. Introduced Union Territories. Amended numerous articles and schedules.

title: Constitution (8th Amendment) Act, 1960
description: The 8th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1960. Extended the period of reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Anglo-Indians in the House of the People and State Assemblies for ten more years (until 1970).

title: Constitution (9th Amendment) Act, 1960
description: The 9th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1960. Made minor adjustments to Indian territory consequent to an agreement with Pakistan on border demarcation of Berubari Union and exchange of certain enclaves.

title: Constitution (10th Amendment) Act, 1961
description: The 10th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1961. Incorporated Dadra and Nagar Haveli (freed from Portuguese rule in 1954) as a Union Territory of India.

title: Constitution (11th Amendment) Act, 1961
description: The 11th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1961. Changed the procedure of election of the Vice-President by replacing the joint meeting of both Houses with an Electoral College. Provided that election of President or Vice-President cannot be challenged on grounds of vacancy in the Electoral College.

title: Constitution (12th Amendment) Act, 1962
description: The 12th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1962. Incorporated Goa, Daman and Diu into the Indian Union as a Union Territory following liberation from Portuguese control.

title: Constitution (13th Amendment) Act, 1962
description: The 13th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1962. Created the State of Nagaland with special provisions under new Article 371A protecting Naga customary law, religious and social practices, and land ownership.

title: Constitution (14th Amendment) Act, 1962
description: The 14th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1962. Incorporated Pondicherry into India as a Union Territory. Created legislatures for Himachal Pradesh, Tripura, Manipur, and Goa, Daman and Diu.

title: Constitution (15th Amendment) Act, 1963
description: The 15th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1963. Raised the retirement age of High Court judges from 60 to 62 years. Made other amendments for clarification regarding High Court jurisdiction.

title: Constitution (16th Amendment) Act, 1963
description: The 16th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1963. Empowered the State to impose further restrictions on fundamental rights in the interest of sovereignty and integrity of India. Made taking oath of allegiance compulsory for candidates in elections.

title: Constitution (17th Amendment) Act, 1964
description: The 17th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1964. Amended Article 31A to include estate and ryotwari land under state acquisition protection. Added 44 more Acts to the Ninth Schedule.

title: Constitution (18th Amendment) Act, 1966
description: The 18th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1966. Clarified that the term 'State' in Article 3 includes Union Territories. Empowered Parliament to form new states by separation from Union Territories.

title: Constitution (19th Amendment) Act, 1966
description: The 19th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1966. Abolished election tribunals and transferred jurisdiction over election disputes to regular High Courts.

title: Constitution (20th Amendment) Act, 1966
description: The 20th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1966. Validated certain appointments of district judges in Uttar Pradesh that were made irregularly.

title: Constitution (21st Amendment) Act, 1967
description: The 21st Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1967. Included Sindhi as the 15th language in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution.

title: Constitution (22nd Amendment) Act, 1969
description: The 22nd Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1969. Enabled the creation of an autonomous state within Assam comprising tribal areas (Meghalaya). Inserted new Article 244A.

title: Constitution (23rd Amendment) Act, 1970
description: The 23rd Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1970. Extended the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in Lok Sabha and State Assemblies for another ten years (until 1980). Also extended special representation for Anglo-Indians.

title: Constitution (24th Amendment) Act, 1971
description: The 24th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1971. Affirmed Parliament's power to amend any part of the Constitution including fundamental rights. Made it obligatory for the President to give assent to a Constitution Amendment Bill.

title: Constitution (25th Amendment) Act, 1971
description: The 25th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1971. Curtailed the fundamental right to property. Provided that any law giving effect to Directive Principles in Article 39(b) and (c) cannot be challenged for violating Articles 14, 19, and 31. Inserted Article 31C.

title: Constitution (26th Amendment) Act, 1971
description: The 26th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1971. Abolished the privy purses and privileges of the former rulers of princely states. Inserted Articles 363A.

title: Constitution (27th Amendment) Act, 1971
description: The 27th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1971. Reorganized the northeastern territories. Created Mizoram and Arunachal Pradesh as Union Territories with legislatures.

title: Constitution (28th Amendment) Act, 1972
description: The 28th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1972. Rationalized the service conditions of ICS (Indian Civil Service) officers and removed their special privileges. Empowered Parliament to determine their service conditions.

title: Constitution (29th Amendment) Act, 1972
description: The 29th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1972. Added two Kerala land reform Acts to the Ninth Schedule for protection from judicial review.

title: Constitution (30th Amendment) Act, 1972
description: The 30th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1972. Changed the basis of appeal to the Supreme Court in civil cases from the value of the subject matter to substantial questions of law of general importance.

title: Constitution (31st Amendment) Act, 1973
description: The 31st Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1973. Increased the elected strength of the Lok Sabha from 525 to 545. Increased the maximum representation from states from 500 to 525 and from Union Territories from 25 to 20.

title: Constitution (32nd Amendment) Act, 1974
description: The 32nd Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1974. Added Article 371D and 371E for special provisions for Andhra Pradesh, protecting rights of people of Telangana region and establishing a Central University.

title: Constitution (33rd Amendment) Act, 1974
description: The 33rd Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1974. Amended Articles 101 and 190 to provide that a member's resignation shall not take effect until accepted by the Speaker/Chairman, to prevent coerced resignations.

title: Constitution (34th Amendment) Act, 1974
description: The 34th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1974. Added 20 more state land reform Acts to the Ninth Schedule for protection from judicial review.

title: Constitution (35th Amendment) Act, 1975
description: The 35th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1975. Replaced the status of Sikkim as a protected state with the status of an associate state. Added Schedule 10 (later replaced). Inserted Article 2A.

title: Constitution (36th Amendment) Act, 1975
description: The 36th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1975. Made Sikkim a full state of the Indian Union (22nd state). Amended the First and Fourth Schedules. Repealed Article 2A inserted by 35th Amendment.

title: Constitution (37th Amendment) Act, 1975
description: The 37th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1975. Provided for a Legislative Assembly for the Union Territory of Arunachal Pradesh with special provisions.

title: Constitution (38th Amendment) Act, 1975
description: The 38th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1975. Made the declaration of Emergency by the President and the promulgation of Ordinances by the President and Governors non-justiciable (beyond judicial review).

title: Constitution (39th Amendment) Act, 1975
description: The 39th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1975. Placed disputes regarding election of the President, Vice-President, Prime Minister, and Speaker beyond the jurisdiction of courts. Later partially struck down by the Supreme Court in Indira Nehru Gandhi v. Raj Narain.

title: Constitution (40th Amendment) Act, 1976
description: The 40th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1976. Empowered Parliament to specify the limits of territorial waters, continental shelf, exclusive economic zone, and maritime zones of India. Added 64 more Acts to Ninth Schedule.

title: Constitution (41st Amendment) Act, 1976
description: The 41st Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1976. Raised the retirement age of members and chairmen of State Public Service Commissions from 60 to 62 years.

title: Constitution (42nd Amendment) Act, 1976
description: The 42nd Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1976. The most sweeping amendment, enacted during the Emergency. Added 'Socialist' and 'Secular' to the Preamble. Added Fundamental Duties (Article 51A, Part IVA). Curtailed the power of judicial review. Made Directive Principles enforceable over Fundamental Rights. Changed Article 368 to prevent judicial review of constitutional amendments. Added Articles 31D, 32A, 39A, 43A, 48A, 131A, 139A, 144A, 226A, 228A. Created Part IVA. Several provisions later struck down by the Supreme Court in Minerva Mills (1980) and partially reversed by the 43rd and 44th Amendments.

title: Constitution (43rd Amendment) Act, 1978
description: The 43rd Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1978. Reversed several provisions of the 42nd Amendment that had curtailed civil liberties. Restored the power of the Supreme Court and High Courts. Repealed Articles 31D and 32A. Restored Article 19 protections.

title: Constitution (44th Amendment) Act, 1978
description: The 44th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1978. Eliminated the Right to Property as a Fundamental Right (repealed Article 31, converted to legal right under Article 300A). Restored safeguards against misuse of Emergency provisions — required 'armed rebellion' instead of 'internal disturbance' for Emergency. Restored the right of the media to report parliamentary proceedings. Made President bound by Cabinet advice for Emergency proclamation.

title: Constitution (45th Amendment) Act, 1980
description: The 45th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1980. Extended the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Anglo-Indians in legislatures for another ten years (until 1990).

title: Constitution (46th Amendment) Act, 1982
description: The 46th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1982. Amended Articles 269 and 286 to reform the taxation of the sale of goods in inter-state trade, ensuring states could levy consignment taxes.

title: Constitution (47th Amendment) Act, 1984
description: The 47th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1984. Added 14 more Acts (mostly state land reform Acts) to the Ninth Schedule.

title: Constitution (48th Amendment) Act, 1984
description: The 48th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1984. Inserted Article 356(5) to permit extension of President's Rule in Punjab beyond one year up to a maximum of two years.

title: Constitution (49th Amendment) Act, 1984
description: The 49th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1984. Extended the protection of the Sixth Schedule to tribal areas in Tripura. Recognized Tripura Tribal Areas Autonomous District Council.

title: Constitution (50th Amendment) Act, 1984
description: The 50th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1984. Inserted Article 33(a) to restrict fundamental rights of persons serving in forces charged with maintenance of public order, protection of essential services and installations.

title: Constitution (51st Amendment) Act, 1984
description: The 51st Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1984. Provided reservation of seats in the Lok Sabha for Scheduled Tribes in Meghalaya, Arunachal Pradesh, Mizoram, and Nagaland. Provided reservation in State Assemblies of these northeastern states.

title: Constitution (52nd Amendment) Act, 1985
description: The 52nd Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1985. Enacted the anti-defection law by adding the Tenth Schedule. A member of Parliament or State Legislature who voluntarily gives up membership of the political party on whose ticket they were elected or votes contrary to party direction is disqualified. Later amended by the 91st Amendment.

title: Constitution (53rd Amendment) Act, 1986
description: The 53rd Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1986. Inserted Article 371G providing special provisions for the State of Mizoram protecting Mizo customary law, religious and social practices, and land ownership.

title: Constitution (54th Amendment) Act, 1986
description: The 54th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1986. Amended Articles 125 and 221 to provide for increased salaries of judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts, and empowered Parliament to determine them by law.

title: Constitution (55th Amendment) Act, 1986
description: The 55th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1986. Inserted Article 371H with special provisions for Arunachal Pradesh, granting the Governor special responsibility with respect to law and order.

title: Constitution (56th Amendment) Act, 1987
description: The 56th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1987. Made provisions for the formation of the State of Goa from the Union Territory. Daman and Diu continued as a separate Union Territory.

title: Constitution (57th Amendment) Act, 1987
description: The 57th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1987. Extended reservation of seats for Scheduled Tribes in the legislatures of Nagaland, Meghalaya, Mizoram, and Arunachal Pradesh.

title: Constitution (58th Amendment) Act, 1987
description: The 58th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1987. Inserted Article 394A empowering the President to publish the authoritative text of the Constitution in Hindi.

title: Constitution (59th Amendment) Act, 1988
description: The 59th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1988. Permitted the proclamation of Emergency in Punjab on grounds of internal disturbance. Extended the maximum duration of President's Rule in Punjab to three years.

title: Constitution (60th Amendment) Act, 1988
description: The 60th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1988. Increased the ceiling on profession tax from Rs 250 to Rs 2,500 per annum under Article 276.

title: Constitution (61st Amendment) Act, 1989
description: The 61st Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1989. Reduced the voting age from 21 years to 18 years for elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies by amending Article 326.

title: Constitution (62nd Amendment) Act, 1989
description: The 62nd Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1989. Extended the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Anglo-Indians for another ten years (until 2000).

title: Constitution (63rd Amendment) Act, 1990
description: The 63rd Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1990. Repealed the special provisions relating to Punjab inserted by the 59th Amendment. Restored the normal constitutional provisions for Punjab.

title: Constitution (64th Amendment) Act, 1990
description: The 64th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1990. Extended President's Rule in Punjab. Permitted President's Rule to continue for a total of three and a half years.

title: Constitution (65th Amendment) Act, 1990
description: The 65th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1990. Replaced the Special Officer for Scheduled Castes and Tribes with a multi-member National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes under amended Article 338. Gave the Commission constitutional status and investigatory powers.

title: Constitution (66th Amendment) Act, 1990
description: The 66th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1990. Added 55 more land reform Acts to the Ninth Schedule.

title: Constitution (67th Amendment) Act, 1990
description: The 67th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1990. Extended President's Rule in Punjab. Permitted it to continue for a total of four years.

title: Constitution (68th Amendment) Act, 1991
description: The 68th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1991. Extended President's Rule in Punjab to five years (the maximum permitted).

title: Constitution (69th Amendment) Act, 1991
description: The 69th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1991. Inserted Articles 239AA and 239AB providing for a Legislative Assembly, Council of Ministers, and special status for the National Capital Territory of Delhi.

title: Constitution (70th Amendment) Act, 1992
description: The 70th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1992. Included the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of Delhi and Pondicherry in the Electoral College for the election of the President.

title: Constitution (71st Amendment) Act, 1992
description: The 71st Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1992. Added Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali as official languages in the Eighth Schedule, bringing the total to 18 languages.

title: Constitution (72nd Amendment) Act, 1992
description: The 72nd Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1992. Provided reservation of seats for Scheduled Tribes in the Tripura State Legislative Assembly until readjustment of seats on the basis of the first census after the year 2000.

title: Constitution (73rd Amendment) Act, 1992
description: The 73rd Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1992. Inserted Part IX (Articles 243-243O) providing constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions. Mandated regular elections, reservation for SCs/STs and women (one-third seats), State Election Commission, and State Finance Commission.

title: Constitution (74th Amendment) Act, 1993
description: The 74th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1993. Inserted Part IXA (Articles 243P-243ZG) providing constitutional status to municipalities and urban local bodies. Mandated regular elections, reservations, and Ward Committees. Added the Twelfth Schedule listing 18 subjects for municipalities.

title: Constitution (75th Amendment) Act, 1994
description: The 75th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1994. Inserted Article 136A (renumbered) enabling state-level Rent Tribunals to reduce burden on regular courts. Also amended Article 338 regarding reports of the National Commission for SCs/STs.

title: Constitution (76th Amendment) Act, 1994
description: The 76th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1994. Added the Tamil Nadu Backward Classes, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Reservation of Seats in Educational Institutions and of Appointments or Posts in the Services under the State) Act, 1993 to the Ninth Schedule, enabling Tamil Nadu to continue 69% reservation.

title: Constitution (77th Amendment) Act, 1995
description: The 77th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1995. Inserted clause (4A) in Article 16 to protect reservations in promotion for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in government services.

title: Constitution (78th Amendment) Act, 1995
description: The 78th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1995. Added further land reform Acts to the Ninth Schedule, bringing the total number of Acts in the Ninth Schedule to 284.

title: Constitution (79th Amendment) Act, 1999
description: The 79th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1999. Extended the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Anglo-Indians for another ten years (until 2010).

title: Constitution (80th Amendment) Act, 2000
description: The 80th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 2000. Implemented the recommendations of the Tenth Finance Commission relating to distribution of net tax proceeds between the Union and the States. Replaced Article 269 and substituted Article 270 for simplified tax sharing.

title: Constitution (81st Amendment) Act, 2000
description: The 81st Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 2000. Inserted Article 16(4B) to provide that unfilled reserved vacancies for SCs/STs shall be treated as a separate class of vacancies and not subject to the 50% reservation ceiling.

title: Constitution (82nd Amendment) Act, 2000
description: The 82nd Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 2000. Inserted a proviso to Article 335 to permit relaxation of qualifying marks and lowering of evaluation standards for SC/ST candidates in promotion.

title: Constitution (83rd Amendment) Act, 2000
description: The 83rd Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 2000. Exempted Arunachal Pradesh from the requirement to provide reservation for Scheduled Castes in Panchayati Raj institutions under Article 243D, as the state had no Scheduled Caste population.

title: Constitution (84th Amendment) Act, 2001
description: The 84th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 2001. Extended the freeze on the delimitation of parliamentary and state assembly constituencies based on the 1971 census until after the first census after 2026. Used 1991 census for SC/ST reservation of constituencies.

title: Constitution (85th Amendment) Act, 2001
description: The 85th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 2001. Inserted the words 'with consequential seniority' in Article 16(4A) to provide for consequential seniority in promotion by reservation for SC/ST government employees.

title: Constitution (86th Amendment) Act, 2002
description: The 86th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 2002. Inserted Article 21A making Right to Education a Fundamental Right for children aged 6-14 years. Added clause 51A(k) making it a Fundamental Duty of parents to provide education. Amended Article 45 to focus on early childhood care for children below 6 years.

title: Constitution (87th Amendment) Act, 2003
description: The 87th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 2003. Provided that for the purposes of readjustment of parliamentary constituencies, population means the population as ascertained at the 2001 census and not any subsequent census.

title: Constitution (88th Amendment) Act, 2003
description: The 88th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 2003. Inserted Articles 268A (since superseded by 101st Amendment) relating to service tax. Provided that service tax shall be levied by the Union but collected and appropriated by both Union and States.

title: Constitution (89th Amendment) Act, 2003
description: The 89th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 2003. Bifurcated the National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes into two separate bodies: the National Commission for Scheduled Castes (Article 338) and the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (Article 338A).

title: Constitution (90th Amendment) Act, 2003
description: The 90th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 2003. Provided that the representation of Scheduled Tribes and non-Scheduled Tribes in the Bodoland Territorial Areas District in the Assam Legislative Assembly shall be maintained as before the creation of the Bodoland Territory.

title: Constitution (91st Amendment) Act, 2003
description: The 91st Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 2003. Strengthened the anti-defection law. Limited the size of the Council of Ministers to 15% of total members of the House. Made the entire provisions relating to disqualification applicable to members of the Tenth Schedule.

title: Constitution (92nd Amendment) Act, 2004
description: The 92nd Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 2004. Added four languages — Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santhali — to the Eighth Schedule, bringing the total number of scheduled languages to 22.

title: Constitution (93rd Amendment) Act, 2006
description: The 93rd Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 2006. Inserted clause (5) in Article 15 enabling the State to make special provisions for advancement of socially and educationally backward classes or SCs/STs regarding admission to educational institutions including private (aided and unaided) institutions, except minority educational institutions. Enabled 27% OBC reservation in higher education.

title: Constitution (94th Amendment) Act, 2006
description: The 94th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 2006. Provided that a Minister for Tribal Welfare shall be appointed in the newly created States of Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand (in addition to the existing states of Madhya Pradesh and Orissa).

title: Constitution (95th Amendment) Act, 2009
description: The 95th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 2009. Extended the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies, and the representation of Anglo-Indians by nomination, for another ten years (until 2020).

title: Constitution (96th Amendment) Act, 2011
description: The 96th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 2011. Substituted 'Odia' for 'Oriya' in the Eighth Schedule as the name of the official language.

title: Constitution (97th Amendment) Act, 2011
description: The 97th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 2011. Inserted Part IXB (Articles 243ZH to 243ZT) relating to co-operative societies, giving constitutional status and protection to co-operative societies. Added 'co-operative societies' after 'unions and associations' in Article 19(1)(c). Part IXB was partially struck down by the Supreme Court in 2021 as it impinged on state legislative competence.

title: Constitution (98th Amendment) Act, 2012
description: The 98th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 2012. Inserted Article 371J empowering the Governor of Karnataka to take special steps for the development of the Hyderabad-Karnataka region, including reservation in education and government employment.

title: Constitution (99th Amendment) Act, 2014
description: The 99th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 2014. Sought to replace the collegium system of appointing judges with a National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC) by amending Articles 124 and 217 and inserting Articles 124A, 124B, 124C. Struck down by the Supreme Court in October 2015 as unconstitutional for violating judicial independence.

title: Constitution (100th Amendment) Act, 2015
description: The 100th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 2015. Facilitated the exchange of certain territories between India and Bangladesh pursuant to the 1974 Land Boundary Agreement and its 2011 Protocol. Amended the First Schedule.

title: Constitution (101st Amendment) Act, 2016
description: The 101st Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 2016. Introduced the Goods and Services Tax (GST) regime. Inserted Articles 246A, 269A, and 279A. Established the GST Council. Subsumed multiple indirect taxes into a unified national tax. One of the most significant economic reforms through constitutional amendment.

title: Constitution (102nd Amendment) Act, 2018
description: The 102nd Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 2018. Inserted Article 338B granting constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes. Inserted Article 342A empowering the President to specify socially and educationally backward classes for each state.

title: Constitution (103rd Amendment) Act, 2019
description: The 103rd Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 2019. Inserted clauses (6) in Articles 15 and 16 to provide up to 10% reservation in education and government employment for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) of citizens other than SC/ST/OBC categories.

title: Constitution (104th Amendment) Act, 2019
description: The 104th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 2019. Extended the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies for another ten years (until 2030). Removed the reserved seats for Anglo-Indians in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies by deleting the relevant provisions.

title: Constitution (105th Amendment) Act, 2021
description: The 105th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 2021. Amended Articles 338B and 342A to restore the power of state governments to identify and maintain their own lists of Socially and Educationally Backward Classes (SEBCs). Clarified that the central list under Article 342A does not prevent states from making their own lists.

title: Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023
description: The 106th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 2023. Inserted Articles 330A, 332A, and 334A to reserve one-third of seats for women in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies. The reservation will be effective after a delimitation exercise conducted following the first census after the commencement of this Act. The reservation is for a period of 15 years but can be extended by Parliament.
